new_entities.name: Self-directed internet CBT
new_entities.description: Internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy completed largely as self-help, with little or no therapist guidance.

new_entities.name: Depression severity
new_entities.description: Severity of depressive symptoms measured with validated clinician-rated or self-report scales.

edges.effect_quant: The most direct long-term depression synthesis is the 2023 JMIR Mental Health meta-analysis, where self-help internet CBT reduced depressive symptoms versus control at follow-up (SMD -0.43, 95% CI -0.67 to -0.20).
edges.population: adults with depressive symptoms or depressive disorders using self-help or minimally guided internet CBT programs
edges.mechanism: Self-directed internet CBT aims to lower depressive symptom burden by teaching cognitive restructuring, behavioral activation, and relapse-prevention skills in a scalable format. Even without regular therapist contact, repeated exposure to structured CBT modules can improve coping and reduce depressive inertia.
edges.summary: The evidence is more solid than the phrase 'self-help' might suggest. Across randomized syntheses, self-directed internet CBT usually outperforms control conditions for depressive symptom reduction, though effects are smaller than in therapist-supported formats.
edges.caveats: Adherence is a real constraint, and some of the strongest long-term data combine self-directed and minimally guided programs. This edge is best interpreted as scalable benefit with modest average effects, not as a full substitute for every patient who would otherwise need clinician-led care.

evidence.citation: MamukashviliDelauM et al 2023 JMIR Ment Health
evidence.notes: Long-Term Efficacy of Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Self-Help Programs for Adults With Depression: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

effect_quant.comparator: self-help internet CBT versus control on long-term depressive symptoms

evidence.citation: ZainalNH et al 2024 Clin Psychol Rev
evidence.notes: Do the effects of internet-delivered cognitive-behavioral therapy (i-CBT) last after a year and beyond? A meta-analysis of 154 randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

effect_quant.comparator: self-guided internet CBT versus control on depressive symptoms at one year or longer
